query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, high-temperature degradation in oxidizing and reducing gases is governed by short-circuit diffusion and selective reactivity along the AM solidification-cell/grain-boundary network that is enriched in Ti and Al. Along these fast paths, Ti/Al react first (forming TiO2/TiN/TiC internally or mixed oxides) and locally deplete Cr, preventing a continuous, protective chromia/alumina scale and driving internal reaction fronts, Kirkendall voiding, and boundary embrittlement. Catastrophic failure occurs when a percolating network of reacted, porous, and embrittled boundaries connects the surface to the interior, enabling rapid crack nucleation and coalescence under residual or applied stress (often coincident with breakaway oxidation or scale spallation).
generation.material_initial_state: As-built laser powder-bed fused Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA with an fcc matrix, exhibiting a cellular/columnar solidification substructure, Ti/Al microsegregation to cell- and grain-boundary regions, residual tensile stresses, and some lack-of-fusion/gas porosity.
generation.intervention: Remove segregation and close porosity prior to exposure via a full-solution homogenization (e.g., 1180–1220 °C for 1–4 h, rapid quench) followed by hot isostatic pressing (HIP; e.g., 1150–1200 °C, 100–150 MPa, 2–4 h) to reduce short-circuit diffusion paths while maintaining the same bulk composition; no surface coating.
generation.conditions: Isothermal exposures at 800–1000 °C for 10–100 h in: (i) dry oxidizing gas (air or O2, pO2 ≈ 0.21 atm, H2O < 100 ppm); (ii) wet oxidizing gas (O2 with 10% H2O by volume); (iii) strongly reducing gas (dry H2, pO2 < 10^-20 atm); and (iv) carburizing/nitriding reducing gas (H2 + 5–10% CH4 or H2 + 10% NH3). Mechanical state: either stress-free (free-standing coupons) or under a constant small bending load to reveal cracking susceptibility.
generation.structural_mediator: A percolating network of AM solidification-cell and grain boundaries enriched in Ti/Al and containing residual porosity that acts as a short-circuit diffusion pathway and preferred reaction site for selective oxidation, nitridation, or carburization.
generation.mechanism: At elevated temperature, Ti and Al at boundary networks react first with the environment. In oxidizing gases, selective boundary oxidation forms Ti-rich mixed oxides internally and depletes Cr near the surface, interrupting chromia/alumina scale continuity and creating sub-surface voids by unbalanced cation/anion fluxes (Kirkendall porosity). In wet O2, chromia volatilization further destabilizes the scale, accelerating breakaway oxidation. In reducing carburizing/nitriding gases, fast boundary transport promotes TiC/TiN precipitation networks and local dealloying. These boundary reactions embrittle and weaken load-bearing paths; once a percolating reacted zone forms from the surface inward, cracks nucleate and coalesce rapidly, producing catastrophic failure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-built baseline, the homogenized+HIP material will: (a) in dry O2 at 900 °C, exhibit a lower oxidation parabolic rate constant (kp) by approximately 2–5× and reduced internal oxidation depth by ~50–80%; (b) show a more continuous chromia-rich surface scale with fewer Ti-rich internal oxides; (c) delay the onset of crack initiation and/or spallation by roughly 3–10× in exposure time; (d) in wet O2 (10% H2O) at 900 °C, still degrade faster overall, but the treated material will postpone breakaway oxidation and spallation relative to baseline and show fewer/broader spall events; (e) in H2 + CH4 or H2 + NH3 at 900 °C, form markedly fewer continuous boundary TiC/TiN networks and retain >20–40% more tensile strength/ductility after 50 h than baseline. If catastrophic failure in the baseline occurs, it will initiate along reacted boundary networks; in the treated material, failure (if any) will occur later and be less boundary-localized.
generation.baseline: As-built specimens without homogenization/HIP, tested under the same temperatures, gas compositions, durations, and mechanical loading. Expected baseline behavior: higher kp, earlier breakaway oxidation/spallation in oxidizing gases, deeper internal oxidation, rapid boundary TiC/TiN formation in carburizing/nitriding gases, and earlier crack initiation/strength loss originating along boundary networks.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis applies when: (1) AM-induced boundary/cellular segregation and porosity are present; (2) temperatures are high enough for bulk and boundary diffusion (≈≥700 °C) but below temperatures causing melting or extensive phase dissolution; (3) Al content is insufficient to form a continuous external alumina scale (as expected at Al0.2), so chromia/mixed oxides dominate; (4) water vapor partial pressure is not negligible (which accelerates chromia volatilization) but is controllable. It may not apply at T ≤ 650 °C (kinetics too slow), at very high Al contents that form continuous alumina, or if a dense, continuous environmental barrier coating removes gas access to boundaries.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitudes (e.g., exact kp reduction, time-to-failure factors) are uncertain and may vary with precise heat-treatment schedule, grain size changes from HIP/homogenization, and powder-derived impurities (e.g., S, O, N). The relative roles of Ti vs Cr in scale breakdown and the contribution of hydrogen-assisted decohesion in dry H2 (absent carburizing/nitriding species) are also uncertain without direct measurement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare matched AM coupons from the same build. Group A: as-built. Group B: homogenized (≈1200 °C/2 h, water quench) + HIP (≈1180 °C/2 h, 120 MPa). Expose both groups at 900 °C for 50 h in: (i) dry O2; (ii) O2 + 10% H2O; (iii) H2 + 10% CH4; and optionally (iv) dry H2. Track mass change in situ (TGA) and log spallation events. After exposure, section and characterize cross-sections (SEM/EDS/EBSD) for internal reaction product depth and continuity along boundaries, quantify porosity (image analysis), and map element depletions (EPMA/SIMS). Perform room-temperature tensile tests and measure crack initiation sites (fractography).
measurements: Parabolic oxidation rate constant kp from TGA in dry O2 and wet O2
Time-to-first spallation event and cumulative spall mass
Depth and area fraction of internal oxides/carbides/nitrides along boundaries (image analysis)
Continuity of external Cr-rich scale vs mixed oxides (XRD/EDS line scans)
Elemental depletion profiles (Cr, Ti, Al) near surface and along boundaries (EPMA/SIMS)
Room-temperature tensile strength and elongation retention after exposure
Fractography to identify crack initiation sites (boundary vs transgranular)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, compared to as-built, the homogenized+HIP group does not show (i) a ≥2× reduction in kp in dry O2, (ii) a ≥50% reduction in the depth and continuity of boundary-localized internal reaction products across gases, and (iii) a ≥3× increase in time-to-crack-initiation or first spallation event. It is also falsified if failures in both conditions initiate uniformly within grains rather than along boundaries.
